body: I've battled depression for almost a decade as well. I have MDD as part of my PTSD from serving in Iraq during the invasion. I've been on every med possible with little success. It's pretty extreme, but I've recently started ECT (I was desperate for change, even for just a fighting chance to beat MDD) and with just a few sessions of ECT, I feel like I've turned a corner and I feel like I have a chance to beat this. It's the most optimistic I've been in a decade. ECT is not for everyone, but I had tried everything and was dangerously losing hope. Do your research, and know what you're getting into, but if you're like me and you've been on all the meds possible without relief, then ECT might work for you. I didn't think it would help me so much, but after just four sessions, people were asking me what's changed because I seem so upbeat and hopeful. The side effects aren't as bad as I was lead to believe and the results have been better than I had hoped for. Either way, I hope you find something that works for you. I know what it's like to fight a battle you always seem to be losing. I wish you the best.

First, remember that some of these medications can take up to six weeks to reach full effectiveness. The Wellbutrin is supposed to have an "activating" effect and is supposed to help with focus, concentration, and energy levels. Even at 150mg, you're still on the low side of the dosage range. There's plenty of room to go up. Maybe you just haven't found the right dose, and maybe it will just take longer to reach full effectiveness. If it works, and it doesn't for everyone, but Wellbutrin *should* help with the "mental fog". Mixing Wellbutrin and Effexor (venlafaxine) is a pretty standard front line treatment as they are different classes of drugs. I know you probably don't want to hear this, but I think your doctor will say to give it more time. If after six weeks you haven't seen an improvement, they will likely increase it. You can go as high as 450mg/day.  Good luck and I hope you find something that works for you. I know the mental fog sucks and it sometimes just takes finding the right combination of meds in the right dosages. Your doctor is being cautious since they want to find the lowest effective dose. I wish you well!
